clue.text: Green grass eater swallows the lot

indicators.note: the grass eater takes the other piece down inside itself, so one sits within the other

parts.note: a cow is the classic grazing animal
the lot means all of it

explanation.surface: A grazing animal gobbles up everything in the field.
explanation.definitionFit: Green means inexperienced or raw, the same sense as an immature, untried youth.

clue.text: Worn by some Arab.A yashmak? No, a cloak

indicators.note: only some of the letters of these words are used, a run lying across them

explanation.surface: A puzzled question about Arab dress: is that a veil or a cloak?
explanation.walkthrough: 'some' tells you to take part of 'Arab. A yashmak', where the letters run across the full stop. 'Worn by' just joins the words, and 'No' sets up the surface question.
explanation.definitionFit: An abaya is the long loose robe worn over clothing by many women in Arab countries.

clue.text: Book-keeper has a pound on Rainmaker

parts.note: libra is the Latin pound, the origin of the abbreviation lb

indicators.note: the word rain is made into something new, its letters reformed

explanation.surface: An accountant has bet money on a racehorse called Rainmaker.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Book-keeper' looks like an accountant but means a keeper of books. The clue splits Rainmaker: RAIN is reworked ('maker') into RIAN after LIBRA.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone in charge of a library looks after its books, a witty literal reading of keeper.

clue.text: Doctor who enjoyed an "elementary education ?

parts.note: Sherlock Holmes's medical companion was forever being told things were elementary, so his schooling by the detective was elementary

explanation.surface: A medic who went to primary school.
explanation.walkthrough: Holmes's line 'Elementary, my dear ...' is addressed to his friend the doctor; 'Doctor who' also teases the TV series.
explanation.definitionFit: Holmes's doctor friend and narrator is the man repeatedly told that matters were elementary.

clue.text: Maybe a fish dish a French girl introduced and cooked

indicators.note: the second piece is brought into the girl's name, placed inside it

parts.note: Marie is a typical French girl's name

indicators.note: cooked means the letters of and are prepared afresh in another order

explanation.surface: A French girl brings in and prepares a fish dish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cooked' turns AND into NAD, which goes inside MARIE.
explanation.definitionFit: A seasoned liquid of wine, vinegar and spices in which fish is soaked, or the pickled fish itself.

clue.text: Claims my idea has somehow come into flower

indicators.note: somehow means in some unspecified way, so these letters are put in a different order

explanation.surface: Someone protests that their idea has turned into a flower.
explanation.definitionFit: A Michaelmas daisy is an autumn-flowering aster, blooming around Michaelmas at the end of September.

clue.text: Trust set up by City nail-maker

indicators.note: in a down clue set up means written upwards, so both pieces read backwards

parts.note: EC is the postcode for the City of London
a nailer is someone who makes nails

explanation.surface: A trust has been founded by a City firm of nail manufacturers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'set up' turns ECNAILER round as a whole. In a down clue that means reading it upwards.
explanation.definitionFit: Trust and dependence are synonyms: placing faith in someone.

clue.text: New, but gets shelved by 3

definitions.meaning: new as an adjective, fresh or original
the 3 is the book-keeper: a work of fiction is what such a person puts on shelves

explanation.surface: Something new that is put away on a shelf.
explanation.definitionFit: Novel means original and fresh, and a novel is a book a library keeper shelves.

clue.text: Press worried in face of such spreading abroad

indicators.note: in places the reworked word inside the face

parts.note: the dial is the face of a clock or watch

indicators.note: worried means agitated, so the letters of press are shaken up

explanation.surface: The press is anxious about something spreading overseas.
explanation.walkthrough: 'worried' turns PRESS into SPERS, which goes inside DIAL. 'of such' is only a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Scattering things widely is the act of distribution in all directions.

clue.text: Taking a year off from the Cabal's a bit awkward

indicators.note: awkward means clumsy, so these letters are handled out of order

explanation.surface: Someone takes leave from a secretive clique that is rather uncomfortable to be in.
explanation.definitionFit: An academic's paid year of leave from teaching for study or travel.

clue.text: Five away? That's great!

parts.note: V is the Roman numeral for five
split as a + way, with way giving ST, the abbreviation for street

explanation.surface: Delight that five people have gone.
explanation.walkthrough: Read 'away' as 'a way': A plus ST, short for street. 'That's' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Vast means huge or immense, which is a sense of great.

clue.text: Path of a high ball-a hit returned

indicators.note: returned means sent back, so the whole run is read from right to left

parts.note: a lob is a ball hit high in the air
a rap is a sharp hit

explanation.surface: Describing how a lofted ball travels when a stroke sends it back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'returned' turns round the whole run A LOB A RAP. 'of' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A projectile's curved trajectory follows this mathematical curve.

clue.text: Joined with a student converting 19

parts.note: L is a learner, as on the plates of a learner driver

indicators.note: converting means changing the form of the word that 19 stands for

parts.note: 19 across means out of work, the word idle

explanation.surface: Joining up with a student who is being converted.
explanation.walkthrough: IDLE, the answer to 19, is reworked ('converting') into LIED after A and L.
explanation.definitionFit: Allied means united or associated with another, as nations join in an alliance.

clue.text: Ascetic leaders of youth of Gandhi's India

indicators.note: the leaders of these words are their first letters

explanation.surface: An ascetic guides India's young followers of Gandhi.
explanation.definitionFit: A Hindu holy man devoted to meditation and self-denial.

clue.text: Places for private worship, or a party?

parts.note: the Tories are the British Conservative Party

explanation.surface: Asking whether a venue is for private prayer or for a party.
explanation.walkthrough: 'party' looks like a celebration, but it is a political party, the Conservatives.
explanation.definitionFit: Small chapels set apart for private prayer.

clue.text: Unfortunate, being unable to " Find the lady "?

definitions.meaning: unfortunate in the sense of ill-starred

definitions.text: being unable to " Find the lady "?
definitions.meaning: Find the Lady is the three-card trick, and 'Luck be a lady' says chance is a lady: if you cannot find her you are out of it

explanation.surface: Someone unlucky at the three-card trick, never picking the queen.
explanation.walkthrough: Find the Lady is a street con where you bet on which of three cards is the queen.
explanation.definitionFit: Unfortunate and ill-starred are synonyms, and being without the 'lady' of chance means having none.

clue.text: How meekly a boxer takes the count

definitions.text: How meekly a boxer takes the count

parts.words: How meekly a boxer takes the count
parts.note: a fighter who accepts defeat without resistance stays flat on the canvas while the referee counts

explanation.surface: A boxer submits tamely to being counted out.
explanation.definitionFit: Taking something meekly is accepting it without protest, and a floored boxer stays horizontal for the count.

clue.text: Make no mistake, would you say, with such a tie-up ?

indicators.note: asks how the phrase would be spoken, so the sound of it is what counts

parts.note: to make no mistake is to slip not

explanation.surface: Insisting there must be no error when tying something up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Slip not' sounds the same as the knot, since the k is silent. 'with such a' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A knot that can be undone by a pull on the free end is a kind of tie.

clue.text: I am a long way off-course in a 7 street

indicators.note: way off course means badly astray, so these letters wander out of order

explanation.surface: A navigator admits being far off course along a street in a book.
explanation.walkthrough: 7 is NOVEL: 'Magnolia Street' is a 1932 novel by Louis Golding. 'in' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Louis Golding's Magnolia Street is a once-famous novel named after a Manchester street.

clue.text: Out of work, these hands make mischief.

definitions.meaning: the proverb says the devil finds work for unoccupied hands

explanation.surface: Unemployed people get up to trouble.
explanation.definitionFit: Being jobless means being unoccupied, and the proverb warns that unoccupied hands find mischief.

clue.text: Dippy sort of character

parts.note: dippy looks like silly, but it means someone who takes a dip in the water

explanation.surface: A slightly daft person.
explanation.definitionFit: A swimmer taking a dip in the sea or a pool is literally a dippy character.

clue.text: 19.talk? Scandalous!

parts.note: 19 gives idle: idle talk, often scandalous, about other people's business

explanation.surface: Disapproval of idle talk.
explanation.definitionFit: Chatter about other people's private affairs is idle and often scandalous talk.

clue.text: Captain Kettle should have got on with this

definitions.text: Captain Kettle should have got on with this

parts.words: Captain Kettle should have got on with this
parts.note: a kettle getting up vapour, and a ship's captain getting under way powered by it

explanation.surface: A sea captain should have pressed ahead.
explanation.walkthrough: Captain Kettle was a fictional sea captain in popular adventure stories of the 1890s; a kettle on the boil gives off vapour.
explanation.definitionFit: A boiling kettle gives off water vapour, and steamships were driven by it.

clue.text: Play for drinks ?

definitions.meaning: a game played on a chequered board, the British name for checkers

explanation.surface: Playing a game for rounds of drinks.
explanation.definitionFit: The board game checkers is called by this name in Britain, and gulps of drink are also called this.

clue.text: Jet-propelled gasteropod ?

definitions.meaning: driven by a turbine, as in a turbojet
a genus of sea snail, the turban shells

explanation.surface: A snail that can go at jet speed.
explanation.definitionFit: A turbine-driven engine has this prefix, and it is also the genus name of turban snails.

clue.text: Order the papers

parts.note: to put loose sheets in order is to stack them up in a heap

explanation.surface: An editor tells someone to tidy up the documents.
explanation.definitionFit: Stacking documents neatly one on another makes a heap of them.

clue.text: Such close friends should eschew covetousness

definitions.text: Such close friends should eschew covetousness

parts.words: Such close friends should eschew covetousness
parts.note: the commandment forbids coveting the house, wife or goods of the people next door

explanation.surface: Good friends shouldn't be envious of each other.
explanation.walkthrough: 'close' means near in space: the Tenth Commandment says not to covet what belongs to those living next door.
explanation.definitionFit: People living close by are the subject of the commandment against coveting.

clue.text: I make an effort about some equality measure

indicators.note: the first two pieces go about, around, the next one

parts.note: to try is to make an effort

explanation.surface: Someone works at a way of measuring fairness.
explanation.definitionFit: In geometry, a mapping that keeps distances equal; literally 'equal measure' from Greek.

clue.text: What sort of chance had Hilton's harvest ?

definitions.text: What sort of chance had Hilton's harvest ?

parts.words: What sort of chance had Hilton's harvest ?
parts.note: James Hilton's 1941 novel about an amnesiac soldier names its harvest after mere chance

explanation.surface: Asking how lucky a hotel's crop was.
explanation.walkthrough: James Hilton wrote the novel 'Random Harvest'; 'Hilton' tempts you towards the hotels.
explanation.definitionFit: Chance that follows no pattern is haphazard, the title word of Hilton's novel.
